extraction_method: JSON data artifacts fetched verbatim (no DOM scraping), same-origin, via the page's own fetch() inside evaluate_script, saved through the filePath option. Opened own chrome-devtools page on https://deepswe.datacurve.ai/ in an isolated browser context named deepswe-rescrape-20260915 (page id 3, stable all run except one navigate_page mistake described in notes). Every evaluate_script was paired with select_page in the SAME tool-call turn and began with a location.href guard that THROWS on mismatch, comparing hostname with === not includes. Under contention from other agents sharing the browser the guard fired on several consecutive attempts before winning the race; every one of those was a thrown error, never a value written to disk. File size on disk and a diff against 20260906/deepswe/raw.json were checked after the save. Also navigated the same page (select_page + navigate_page paired) to the page route https://deepswe.datacurve.ai/data/v1.1?hm_stat=avg_duration_seconds&pivot=true to read the hm_stat option list directly out of the rendered <select> elements. No Node/curl fallback.

data_route_probe.method: Navigated the isolated page to this route (select_page + navigate_page paired in one turn, href-guard verified afterward) and read the rendered <select> element option lists and button labels directly from the DOM heatmap-pivot controls.
data_route_probe.finding_a_mean_vs_median: hm_stat exposes only the mean/avg family (avg_cost_usd, avg_steps, avg_input_tokens, avg_output_tokens, avg_peak_context_tokens, avg_duration_seconds) plus counts. It offers no median_* option anywhere. This confirms the task's premise: the page's own publishable-statistic list is the MEAN family, and the artifact's median_* fields (median_cost_usd, median_agent_steps, median_output_tokens, median_input_tokens, median_duration_seconds, median_peak_context_tokens, etc.) are not what the site surfaces as its headline numbers, even though raw.json/normalized.json keep every median_* field verbatim per the task instruction to keep every field.
data_route_probe.finding_b_gaps_hm_stat_vs_artifact: Three hm_stat values have no matching field in the leaderboard-live.json artifact rows, checked field-by-field against the 59-key row schema: (1) total_cost_usd -- absent; only mean_cost_usd and median_cost_usd exist, so a total would have to be derived (e.g. mean_cost_usd * n_attempted) rather than read off the artifact. (2) avg_peak_context_tokens -- absent; the artifact carries median_peak_context_tokens only, no mean variant, which breaks the otherwise-universal mean/median pairing for every other efficiency stat. (3) n_errors -- absent; the artifact has n_attempted, n_passed, ci_attempted, ci_passed but no explicit error/failure count field. These three are genuine gaps between what the page's heatmap can pivot on and what the same-origin JSON artifacts expose; they most likely come from a per-trial dataset backing the heatmap and tasks/trials views that was not found as a separate fetchable artifact (probed candidate paths for it, see artifact_probe, all 404).

cost_adjustment_carried_forward.note: raw.json is byte-for-byte identical to 20260906/deepswe/raw.json (see changes_vs_20260906), so the cost-adjustment mapping measured that day is carried forward unchanged rather than re-derived: 19 of 70 v1.1 configs differ from their raw mean_cost_usd, covering 7 models -- glm-5-3-flash (x0.5), gemini-3-6-flash (x0.5), gpt-5-6-luna (x0.2, all 5 efforts), gpt-5-6-terra (x0.8, all 5 efforts), gpt-5-6-sol (x0.76-0.77, all 5 efforts, effort-dependent), deepseek-v4-pro (x6.90) and deepseek-v4-flash (x4.63, all increases not discounts) -- plus one v1-tab config, mini_swe_agent_deepseek_v4_pro_default, adjusted x0.25. This scrape did not re-verify the adjustment against the server-rendered HTML the way 20260906 did; it is a carry-forward on the strength of the byte-identical artifact, and should be re-observed the next time the artifact actually changes.

MODEL CHECK: 'muse-spark-1.3' is STILL NOT present (only muse-spark-1.2 and muse-spark-1.1 exist). 'claude-fable-5.1' is also NOT present (site has claude-fable-5 only). Both re-verified by scanning the model field of all 230 normalized records this run.

OPERATOR ERROR, corrected: one navigate_page call was issued right after select_page(3) but in a way that let another agent's select_page win the shared pointer first, so navigate_page briefly sent a different agent's page (the livebench-rescrape-20260915 page) to the deepswe data route instead of my own page. Caught immediately via list_pages, and fixed by selecting that page back and navigating it back to its prior URL (https://livebench.ai/#/?showorg=1) before continuing. All subsequent navigate_page and evaluate_script calls paired select_page in the same turn and verified location.href inside the script afterward. Flagging this because navigate_page, unlike evaluate_script, has no pageId parameter and no href guard of its own -- it acts on whatever page is currently selected at call time, so the same-turn pairing discipline matters for it too, not just for evaluate_script.

BROWSER CONTENTION: this scrape ran alongside several other agents on one shared browser instance. Even with select_page and evaluate_script/navigate_page issued in the same turn, the shared 'selected page' pointer was stolen on multiple attempts; each script needed several retries. The throwing href guard is what made evaluate_script safe, since every lost race surfaced as an error instead of another site's data being written to raw.json.

NORMALIZED.JSON: not regenerated field-by-field this run. Because raw.json is byte-for-byte identical to 20260906/deepswe/raw.json (verified by diff), and normalized.json carries no scrape-run-specific field (no per-record scraped_at; every record's generated_at/date already reflects the artifact's own stamp), the transformation from an unchanged input is itself unchanged, so 20260906/deepswe/normalized.json was copied verbatim rather than retyped or re-derived by hand. This is a mechanical file copy of a machine-produced file, not a transcription.
